mathia-agnostic-openalex-v1.label: Agnostic Mathia OpenAlex supplement accepted object

riemann_v1.disposition: Immutable parent lineage; the v2 accepted release governs overlapping evidence and corrections.

openalex_graph.disposition: Identity, citation, discovery, and duplicate/version evidence only; not positive mathematical evidence.

unresolved_canonicalization.candidate: Vasyunin-sum identity for the retained generalized Dedekind-sum correlation
unresolved_canonicalization.reason: The accepted object supports a modified generalized Dedekind sum and its reciprocity law but does not bind that convention to every Vasyunin-sum identity.
The issue lists it only as a granularity example; the selected accepted projection evidence does not support a stable standalone note without fresh analysis.

known_blind_spots: This is a projection of retained accepted analyses, not a claim of bibliographic or mathematical completeness.
The OpenAlex discovery graph contributes identity and citation coverage, but graph membership alone cannot support mathematical prose.
Unprocessed or unavailable source text was not reacquired or mined for new claims; formula-damaged accepted units were summarized only at their audited prose-level boundary.
qwen formalization status is pinned to one repository revision and records availability/status, not independent proof verification by this projection.

sections.what_it_is: A sequence criterion that concentrates zero information into coefficients formed from finite rational combinations of zeta values at positive even integers. The retained Mathia analysis records the RH-scale decay condition, an inversion formula, and an exponential generating function as different views of the same sequence.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas records the asymptotic order condition as bidirectionally equivalent to RH. For Mathia it is a reusable example of compressing analytic zero information into a discrete, algebraically reversible observable.
sections.scope_and_limits: This is an equivalent criterion, not a proof of RH. Direct numerical checks can remain insensitive to hypothetical high off-line zeros, and the retained records report no Lean formalization. It is intentionally distinct from Báez-Duarte's strengthening of the Nyman–Beurling closure criterion.

sections.what_it_is: A functional-analytic reformulation of zero exclusion as a closure or density statement for fractional-part functions. The retained Mathia object also records the wider L^p pattern: the ambient norm parameter tracks a corresponding zero-free half-plane, while a single characteristic-function target can compress the full density question.
sections.relation_to_research: Both retained views classify the L² criterion as equivalent to RH. It is relevant to Mathia as a precise bridge from analytic zero location to approximation and representation selection.
sections.scope_and_limits: Closure membership is not a constructive approximation algorithm. The evidence supplies neither an effective convergence rate nor a Lean proof, and it does not imply that the discrete Baez-Duarte strengthening is automatic.

sections.what_it_is: A strengthening of the Nyman–Beurling closure criterion that restricts the generating family from all real dilation parameters at least one to natural-number dilations. The smaller arithmetic skeleton retains the target membership condition that is equivalent to RH.
sections.relation_to_research: This result shows that the continuum of generators is not essential at the level of closed span. It is useful to Mathia as a precise example of a representation being compressed without losing the decisive property.
sections.scope_and_limits: The theorem statement does not provide a constructive approximating sequence or rate. It is not the Báez-Duarte sequence criterion based on zeta values. The qwen source label `baez-duarte-2002` and Mathia source `baezduarte2003_nyman` are retained as preprint/publication views of arXiv `math/0202141`, not as two mathematical nodes.

sections.what_it_is: A reformulation that orders Farey fractions, compares them with uniform grid positions, and aggregates the resulting discrepancy. The retained Mathia analysis keeps the quadratic and absolute-deviation norms distinct while identifying the common representation change from reduced-rational arithmetic to equidistribution error.
sections.relation_to_research: The retained source unit states RH-equivalent bounds for the discrepancy aggregates. This is directly useful as a prior-art boundary for geometric Mathia routes that merely repackage Farey points or their one-dimensional distribution.
sections.scope_and_limits: The note records the criterion at mechanism level because the retained analysis flags formula and exponent typography as requiring scan verification for literal reuse. A geometric redrawing of the same discrepancy is not new RH progress.

sections.what_it_is: A one-parameter heat-flow deformation of the completed xi function with a threshold Λ separating the real-rooted regime from the regime containing nonreal zeros. The deformation turns a static zero-location question into a boundary problem in function space.
sections.relation_to_research: RH is equivalent to Λ ≤ 0, while the Rodgers–Tao result recorded in both retained views proves the complementary bound Λ ≥ 0. The Mathia analysis treats the contradiction mechanism as a clash between forced local equilibrium under Λ < 0 and known local zero statistics.
sections.scope_and_limits: The proved lower bound does not prove RH; together with RH it would force Λ = 0. Historical numerical bounds in older source units are not treated as current evidence, and no Lean formalization is claimed.

sections.what_it_is: A reformulation of RH as nonnegativity of an explicit-formula zero functional for an admissible class of test functions. It changes the target from locating every zero to proving positivity of a structured family of quantities.
sections.relation_to_research: The retained Mathia interpretation records the positivity statement as equivalent to RH and treats it as a central bridge between prime-zero duality and operator or geometric positivity programs.
sections.scope_and_limits: Equivalence does not explain why the functional should be nonnegative. Admissibility and normalization choices are mathematically substantive; the note does not generalize positivity beyond the retained test-function setting or claim a proof.

sections.what_it_is: A discrete positivity reformulation in which coefficients associated with the completed zeta function can be expressed through its zeros and through derivatives of log xi at a distinguished point.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas records nonnegativity of every Li coefficient as equivalent to RH. Mathia's accepted analysis places the sequence beside Weil positivity as a compression from a functional family to discrete quantities.
sections.scope_and_limits: The criterion does not establish positivity, and the retained qwen record reports no located Lean proof. This note does not reconstruct formula-sensitive coefficient definitions beyond the accepted source descriptions.

sections.what_it_is: A conditional spectral strategy seeking a self-adjoint operator whose real spectrum corresponds exactly to the ordinates of nontrivial zeta zeros. Retained statistical and periodic-orbit correspondences act as constraints on the missing system rather than as its construction.
sections.relation_to_research: An exact self-adjoint realization with the required spectral identification would force the corresponding zeros onto the critical line. Mathia uses the program as a model of a potentially fertile representation whose proof value depends on the representation enforcing reality.
sections.scope_and_limits: No operator, domain, boundary conditions, or exact spectral identification is supplied by the retained evidence. Random-matrix statistics and prime/orbit analogies do not themselves prove RH.

sections.what_it_is: A conjectural fine-scale law for pairs of high zeta-zero ordinates after normalization by their local density. The retained Mathia material separates Montgomery's proved, RH-conditional restricted Fourier regime from the extrapolation that yields the full pair-correlation law and unitary symmetry prediction.
sections.relation_to_research: The conjecture supplies a discriminating zero-statistics target and constrains spectral analogies. It also enters the retained de Bruijn–Newman argument as known local-statistical input against an overly rigid equilibrium consequence.
sections.scope_and_limits: The qwen atlas explicitly records no implication from the statistical similarity to RH. The full law is conjectural; restricted conditional results, numerical evidence, and a hypothetical exact operator are distinct epistemic claims.

sections.what_it_is: A family of exact identities expressing weighted prime-counting data through the pole and zeros of zeta together with local correction terms. In the retained Mathia view, a transform places the same test function on the prime and zero sides; the function-field analogue admits a Lefschetz trace interpretation.
sections.relation_to_research: The explicit formula is a central bridge rather than an RH equivalence by itself. It makes proposed spectral, positivity, and geometric mechanisms answerable against the exact arithmetic terms they must reproduce.
sections.scope_and_limits: The identity does not force critical-line zero location. Test-function hypotheses, smoothing, local terms, signs, and convergence cannot be dropped, and qwen reports no located complete Lean proof of the theorem family.

sections.what_it_is: A family of proved regions excluding zeta zeros near the line Re(s)=1. The retained Mathia source describes the mechanism as converting upper bounds for zeta into a forbidden region and distinguishes the classical inverse-log boundary from the stronger Vinogradov–Korobov-scale shape.
sections.relation_to_research: Zero-free regions give unconditional partial control of zeros and support quantitative prime-number-theorem error bounds. They are a classical-method baseline for any proposed Mathia route that claims only near-one exclusion.
sections.scope_and_limits: These regions are strictly weaker than RH and do not locate every nontrivial zero on the critical line. Exact constants and formula-sensitive boundaries are not reconstructed from OCR-damaged passages. qwen records only verified components in an external Lean project, not a complete formalization of every historical refinement.

nodes.canonical_name: Finite-field Riemann hypothesis via Frobenius cohomology

sections.what_it_is: In the zeta theory of varieties over finite fields, reciprocal zeros and poles are interpreted as Frobenius eigenvalues on étale cohomology, and geometric positivity constrains their magnitudes. The retained curve-level discussion presents Euler product, functional equation, and the finite-field RH as a proved structural package.
sections.relation_to_research: This is a proved analogue and a source of exact roles—Frobenius, cohomology, duality, and positivity—that a classical geometric proposal may try to reproduce. It is one of the strongest retained structural analogies for RH.
sections.scope_and_limits: The function-field theorem does not transfer a proof to the classical Riemann zeta function. The note does not infer that an analogous classical geometric object exists, and it preserves the distinction between zeros themselves and the reciprocal characteristic roots interpreted as eigenvalues.

sections.what_it_is: A noncommutative-geometric spectral program in which zeta or L-function zeros appear as missing states or an absorption spectrum for an idele-class action on adele-class spaces. Retained local and finite-place trace formulas recover corresponding explicit-formula terms, while noncritical zeros are represented as resonances.
sections.relation_to_research: The program aims to make the explicit formula a genuine global trace formula and to explain the sign that obstructs a naive emitted-spectrum picture. It supplies concrete local constructions and a disciplined alternative to a bare Hilbert–Pólya analogy.
sections.scope_and_limits: The retained source explicitly leaves the decisive global trace formula open and does not claim Weil positivity or RH. Local trace results, a spectral interpretation, and a completed global proof are separate statuses.

sections.what_it_is: A method for proving lower bounds on the proportion of zeta zeros on the critical line by multiplying or combining zeta and its derivatives with a tunable Dirichlet-polynomial mollifier. The retained Conrey analysis identifies longer mollifiers, mean-value asymptotics, Kloosterman-sum control, and variational optimization as distinct components.
sections.relation_to_research: It is a classical partial-progress route that demonstrates how representation choice and an auxiliary approximation can make a zero-location problem tractable without resolving all zeros.
sections.scope_and_limits: A positive critical-line proportion is not RH. Claimed improvements depend on the admissible mollifier length and all required twisted-moment or error estimates; an unproved supporting estimate cannot be counted as an achieved bound.

sections.what_it_is: An arithmetic quantum statistical mechanical system in which the Riemann zeta function occurs as thermodynamic counting data and its pole corresponds to a phase transition in the equilibrium-state structure. The retained analysis also records an arithmetic symmetry acting on the low-temperature phases.
sections.relation_to_research: For Mathia this is a concrete bridge from zeta to operator-algebraic dynamics and symmetry. It is relevant as an established realization of arithmetic information, not as a zero criterion.
sections.scope_and_limits: Encoding zeta as a partition function does not locate its nontrivial zeros and does not prove RH. This note does not merge the system with Connes's separate adele-class trace program merely because both use noncommutative geometry.

sections.what_it_is: The historical assertion that the absolute value of the summatory Möbius function stays below the square-root scale. The retained qwen atlas records it specifically to prevent a false stronger statement from being mistaken for a viable open criterion.
sections.relation_to_research: The conjecture would imply RH, so it is a useful negative prior-art node when a Mathia route accidentally strengthens a legitimate Möbius-summatory RH criterion to this false bound.
sections.scope_and_limits: The Mertens conjecture is disproved. Its failure does not disprove RH, and this note does not conflate it with weaker Möbius-summatory conditions that are equivalent to RH.

nodes.canonical_name: Random matrix model for zeta zeros

sections.what_it_is: A statistical analogy between locally unfolded zeta-zero ordinates and eigenvalues from unitary random-matrix ensembles. The retained Montgomery analysis uses an extrapolated form factor and Dyson's comparison to select the unitary symmetry class.
sections.relation_to_research: The model predicts local spacing and correlation behavior and constrains a prospective spectral realization. It provides a transfer laboratory for testing whether a proposed mechanism reflects universal statistics or arithmetic structure specific to zeta.
sections.scope_and_limits: Statistical agreement is not equality of spectra, an operator construction, or an implication of RH. Unfolding removes absolute height and global density information, and the full zeta pair-correlation law remains conjectural.

sections.what_it_is: An inequality involving the divisor-sum function and harmonic numbers, required for every positive integer with a specified equality case. The retained Mathia analysis emphasizes the move from zeta zeros to elementary-looking arithmetic observables.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas and Mathia source both record the inequality as equivalent to RH. It is a useful stress test for whether a change of surface representation has actually reduced difficulty.
sections.scope_and_limits: The criterion is not an elementary proof of RH; its equivalence runs through Robin's criterion and deeper analytic results. No Lean proof of the equivalence is recorded.

sections.what_it_is: A square-root-scale cancellation condition for the summatory Möbius function: the retained qwen entry states the bound with an arbitrary positive epsilon, while Mathia contrasts this sign-cancellation observable with prime-power counting error.
sections.relation_to_research: The condition is bidirectionally equivalent to RH and gives a prime-side cancellation interface that is structurally different from direct zero location.
sections.scope_and_limits: The criterion does not assert the false sharper Mertens bound. Its qwen status is foundations-only rather than a located formal proof of the full equivalence.

sections.what_it_is: A quantitative prime-power counting statement controlling the error of the Chebyshev psi function at square-root scale with logarithmic loss. Mathia treats it as the main-term-error counterpart to Möbius sign cancellation.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas records the stated error bound as equivalent to RH. It is a canonical arithmetic target for explicit-formula routes.
sections.scope_and_limits: This criterion is distinct from the prime-counting Li(x) error form and from finite-range explicit inequalities. None of the retained evidence proves the bound or records a complete Lean formalization.

sections.what_it_is: A growth condition on the Riesz entire function constructed from zeta values. The retained Mathia comparison places its continuous growth behavior beside the discrete decay of the Báez-Duarte coefficients.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas records the specified growth exponent as equivalent to RH. The criterion supplies a continuous representation of the same broad zeta-value information explored by sequence criteria.
sections.scope_and_limits: The direct relation to the Báez-Duarte sequence does not identify the two observables. Numerical oscillation and first-zero dominance are diagnostic representations, not proofs of the required asymptotic bound.

sections.what_it_is: A universal upper bound for the divisor-sum function normalized by n log log n, required above a fixed finite threshold. The retained Mathia analysis places the same normalization beside Gronwall's limiting upper envelope and motivates extremal-number searches.
sections.relation_to_research: The inequality is equivalent to RH. It gives a sparse arithmetic boundary where counterexamples would have to compete with the maximal-order scale.
sections.scope_and_limits: Restricting attention to extremal subsequences is useful only when a retained theorem justifies the reduction. Finite verification or asymptotic envelope information alone does not prove the universal inequality.

sections.what_it_is: A derivative-zero reformulation: RH is encoded by the absence of nonreal zeros of zeta's derivative to the left of the critical line. Retained Mathia analyses treat differentiation as a transfer from zero geometry to critical-point geometry and counting.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas records the derivative-zero condition as bidirectionally equivalent to RH. It is a canonical diagnostic for proposals based on the analytic landscape of zeta.
sections.scope_and_limits: Asymptotic comparisons between counts of zeros of zeta and zeta' do not automatically establish the zero-free condition for every derivative zero. Extensions to other zeta or L-function classes require their own hypotheses.

sections.what_it_is: A square-root-scale error bound comparing the prime-counting function with the logarithmic integral. The retained Mathia equivalence map treats this as a prime-side surface of the same zero-location claim.
sections.relation_to_research: The qwen atlas records the bound as equivalent to RH. It supplies a standard target for any route claiming to turn zero control into prime-distribution accuracy.
sections.scope_and_limits: The logarithmic factor and choice of prime-counting observable are part of the statement. This criterion is not identical to the Chebyshev psi error formulation even though both are RH-equivalent.

sections.what_it_is: The conjecture that every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part one half.
sections.relation_to_research: This is the reference claim whose criteria, analogues, partial results, and proof programs are distinguished throughout the projection.
sections.scope_and_limits: RH remains open in the retained atlas. Equivalent criteria, finite-height checks, statistical evidence, formalized prerequisites, and proved function-field analogues do not constitute a proof of this conjecture.

sections.what_it_is: The factorization of zeta into prime-indexed local factors in its half-plane of absolute convergence. Mathia's accepted view emphasizes that expanding local prime-power data organizes the global Dirichlet coefficients.
sections.relation_to_research: The product is a foundational prime-to-function bridge and explains why prime-local information enters zeta-based research.
sections.scope_and_limits: The Euler product is verified in pinned mathlib according to qwen, but only in its stated convergence domain. Factorization alone does not supply analytic continuation, the functional equation, or critical-line zero location.

sections.what_it_is: The reflection symmetry of the completed zeta function under s mapping to one minus s. Completion adds the archimedean factors needed to expose the symmetry.
sections.relation_to_research: The equation organizes the critical line as the reflection axis and transfers information between the two sides of the strip. Mathia uses completion as a canonical representation change shared across L-function families.
sections.scope_and_limits: The functional equation is verified in pinned mathlib according to qwen, but symmetry alone does not place zeros on the reflection line or identify different L-functions.

sections.what_it_is: The asymptotic law that the prime-counting function is equivalent to x divided by log x. Retained Mathia evidence contrasts analytic Tauberian routes with the Selberg–Erdős elementary proof architecture.
sections.relation_to_research: PNT is weaker than RH and acts as a foundational checkpoint for prime-zero methods. It shows that the same arithmetic theorem can arise through substantially different representations.
sections.scope_and_limits: The qwen atlas records a verified proof in a pinned external Lean project, not a proof of RH. PNT corresponds to boundary zero-freeness and does not give the square-root-scale error required by RH-equivalent criteria.

sections.what_it_is: An asymptotic formula for the number of nontrivial zeta zeros up to height T. Its main term determines the changing macroscopic zero density and therefore the natural scale for local statistics.
sections.relation_to_research: The formula separates total zero abundance from the harder questions of critical-line proportion, multiplicity, and off-line density. It supplies the normalization used in pair-correlation and random-matrix comparisons.
sections.scope_and_limits: Counting all zeros does not show that they lie on the critical line. The qwen atlas records only partial formal components, not verification of the complete formula.

sections.what_it_is: A computer-assisted theorem that every nontrivial zeta zero up to a stated finite height lies on the critical line, supported by an explicit verification protocol.
sections.relation_to_research: Finite checks calibrate zero-evaluation and counting machinery and constrain where a counterexample could first occur.
sections.scope_and_limits: A finite-height result is not evidence for all heights strong enough to prove RH. The qwen atlas classifies this as a computer-assisted literature result and records no Lean formalization of the complete verification.

nodes.canonical_name: Generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions

sections.what_it_is: The conjecture that every nontrivial zero of every Dirichlet L-function has real part one half.
sections.relation_to_research: It generalizes RH and provides the family-level target behind many conditional uniform arithmetic estimates.
sections.scope_and_limits: Dirichlet GRH remains open. A functional equation, verified local factors, or formalized prerequisites do not establish the conjecture for the family.

aliases: Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions

sections.what_it_is: The conjecture that nontrivial zeros of a Dedekind zeta function lie on the critical line.
sections.relation_to_research: It is a number-field generalization of RH and a comparison point for finite-field zeta theorems and explicit-formula programs.
sections.scope_and_limits: This is an open literature-only conjecture in the qwen atlas. The proved finite-field analogue and the Riemann-zeta special case must not be conflated with the number-field statement.

sections.what_it_is: A conjectural sub-polynomial growth bound for zeta on the critical line.
sections.relation_to_research: RH implies this hypothesis, and its growth control is often used as a conditional analytic resource in moment and approximation arguments.
sections.scope_and_limits: Lindelöf is not recorded as equivalent to RH here; the implication runs from RH to the growth statement. It remains an open literature-only conjecture in the qwen atlas.

nodes.canonical_name: Completed xi and Hardy Z representations

sections.what_it_is: Completion and reparameterization package zeta into an entire xi function with visible reflection symmetry and a real-valued Hardy Z function on the critical line.
sections.relation_to_research: The representations expose symmetry, turn critical-line restriction into real-variable data, and support visualization and sign tests without changing the underlying zero information.
sections.scope_and_limits: Completion and reparameterization do not place off-line zeros on the line. The retained unit supports the roles of xi and Z, while damaged formula extraction makes exact normalization details unsuitable for reuse here.

sections.what_it_is: Voronin universality presents vertical translates of zeta as an infinite-dimensional approximation phenomenon; its probabilistic viewpoint studies the distribution of that translation orbit.
sections.relation_to_research: It supplies a conceptual bridge between individual approximation shifts and a distribution over translated functions, a reusable move from pointwise witnesses to orbit-level behavior.
sections.scope_and_limits: Universality and recurrence do not by themselves prove RH. This note records only the retained source unit's denseness and translation-distribution viewpoints, not a stronger equivalence criterion.

sections.what_it_is: After matching mean densities, the zeta-moment model separates a universal random-matrix contribution from an arithmetic factor carrying prime-dependent information.
sections.relation_to_research: The split is a useful example of decomposing a prediction into a transferable structural component and a domain-specific correction once the comparison scale is fixed.
sections.scope_and_limits: The retained evidence distinguishes proved CUE results, numerical or conditional zeta agreement, and conjectural zeta-moment extrapolation. Those statuses must not be collapsed.

sections.what_it_is: A Sonin space imposes matching localization gaps on a function and its Fourier transform; projection onto that space supplies a positive compressed-trace term.
sections.relation_to_research: It exhibits an operator source for positivity at the archimedean place and a bridge from dual localization constraints to a trace inequality.
sections.scope_and_limits: The retained result applies to the stated compactly supported test class and specified transform vanishings. It does not include finite-prime terms or establish the global positivity criterion needed for RH.

sections.what_it_is: A finite correlation of periodic Bernoulli data is represented by a modified generalized Dedekind sum whose cyclic combination obeys a three-term reciprocity relation exposing gcd data.
sections.relation_to_research: It converts oscillatory fractional-part correlations into an arithmetic object with a reciprocity law, illustrating how cyclic synthesis can remove directional dependence and reveal invariants.
sections.scope_and_limits: Exact coefficients are formula-sensitive and are not reproduced from the compact interpretation. The retained evidence supports generalized Dedekind-sum language, not an automatic identification with every Vasyunin-sum convention.

sections.what_it_is: A zero-detecting argument replaces zeros in small regions by a disjunction asserting largeness of one of several auxiliary analytic witnesses.
sections.relation_to_research: Cauchy-Schwarz and mean-square estimates can then turn witness largeness into a zero-count bound, reframing a geometric counting problem as control of auxiliary quantities.
sections.scope_and_limits: The retained unit carries one branch of the method to an explicit upper bound. It is a partial-progress technique, not a proof that all nontrivial zeros lie on the critical line.

sections.what_it_is: A map factors through the quotient by its kernel, separating the information it forgets from the injective map that faithfully retains what remains.
sections.relation_to_research: It provides both a reusable compression move and a falsification test: a proposed equivalence is too coarse if it merges different images and unnecessarily fine if it preserves distinctions already killed by the map.
sections.scope_and_limits: The quotient is canonical relative to the chosen map, not an absolute simplification of the domain. This cross-domain note does not assert a new RH implication.

sections.what_it_is: A separating hyperplane converts disjoint convex feasibility into one affine witness whose sign can be checked over each set.
sections.relation_to_research: It is a reusable bridge from a primal global-exclusion claim to a dual certificate and motivates searching for a supporting direction instead of comparing every cross-pair.
sections.scope_and_limits: Convexity gives the witness its global authority. Interlocking nonconvex components may defeat any single linear separator, and this note asserts no new RH application.

sections.what_it_is: When an operator respects Fourier modes, expansion converts a coupled evolution equation into scalar coefficient evolutions, with boundary data helping select the admissible basis.
sections.relation_to_research: It exemplifies choosing a representation adapted to the operator so that structural components decouple and scale-dependent behavior becomes predictable.
sections.scope_and_limits: Reconstruction remains a separate obligation; nonlinear terms mix frequencies, and weak convergence may not justify termwise differentiation. This note asserts no new RH application.

sections.what_it_is: For a finite-dimensional complex normal operator, an eigenvector and its invariant orthogonal complement permit induction to an orthogonal eigenspace decomposition.
sections.relation_to_research: The proof architecture shows how a local invariant component can create a smaller problem of the same kind while preserving the structure required for iteration.
sections.scope_and_limits: A generic real operator may lack a real eigenline, and an arbitrary operator need not preserve the orthogonal complement. Eigenspaces are canonical, but bases inside repeated eigenspaces are auxiliary.

sections.what_it_is: An endomorphism algebra can give a Morita-equivalent presentation of module geometry while an induced action preserves the stated trace structure.
sections.relation_to_research: It illustrates comparing presentations at the module-category or Morita level, where geometric information may survive even when the concrete algebras differ.
sections.scope_and_limits: The retained interpretation is explicitly an inference from one source unit. It does not identify Morita-equivalent algebras literally or establish a new connection to the Riemann hypothesis.

sections.what_it_is: Moving from a one-direction persistence index to several independent directions destroys the interval decomposition that makes one-parameter persistence compressible as a barcode.
sections.relation_to_research: It is a reusable warning that generalizing the geometry of an index can remove the canonical decomposition underlying a successful representation, creating a structural rather than merely computational obstruction.
sections.scope_and_limits: Changing arrow direction or broadening maps has different consequences from changing the index poset. The retained unit supports this distinction but no new RH application.
